data.name: Baraq
data.gender_notes: Baraq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Baraq is derived from the word ‘Barr’ which means ‘thunder’. The name Baraq signifies the one who has the power to strike with lightning. In Islamic history, Baraq is also believed to be a title of Prophet Yunus (Jonah) as he was saved from the belly of the whale by Allah's mercy. The name Baraq carries the meaning “Thunderbolt, Lightning” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Baraq usually hope their child will grow to embody thunderbolt, lightning and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine intervention and protection.
data.etymology: Baraq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thunderbolt, Lightning.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baraq total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: براق
in_arabic.meaning: براق يعني الضوء أو النور الساطع في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: براق هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ب-ر-ق' الذي يعني الضوء أو النور الساطع. ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الإسراء آية 1: 'سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلاً من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى الذي باركنا حوله لنريه من آياتنا إنه هو السميع البصير'. يرتبط اسم براق بالبرق أو الضوء السريع، وغالبًا ما يوصف به النور أو الإضاءة الربانية. في الثقافة الإسلامية، يحمل الاسم دلالات روحية وإيمانية قوية.

in_urdu.name: براق
in_urdu.meaning: براق کا مطلب ہے روشنی یا مضبوط نور
in_urdu.long_meaning: براق ایک عربی نام ہے جو 'ب-ر-ق' کے روٹ سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے روشنی یا مضبوط نور۔ قرآن مجید میں اس کا ذکر سفر معراج میں ہوا ہے جب رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کو رات کے وقت مسجد الحرام سے مسجد اقصیٰ تک لے جایا گیا۔ اسلامی ثقافت میں، براق نام برق یا تیزی سے چلنے والی روشنی کی علامت ہے، اور اسے الہی نور یا ربانی اشراق کے ساتھ جوڑا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बराक
in_hindi.meaning: बराक का अर्थ है प्रकाश या तीव्र प्रकाश
in_hindi.long_meaning: बराक एक अरबी नाम है जो 'ब-र-क' मूल से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है प्रकाश या तीव्र प्रकाश। यह नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह पैगंबर मुहम्मद के स्वर्गारोहण की यात्रा से जुड़ा है, जिसे इसराइल के नाम से जाना जाता है। इस्लामी संस्कृति में, बराक नाम प्रकाश, ज्ञान और आध्यात्मिक जागृति का प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: براق
in_pashto.meaning: براق د رڼا یا شديدې رڼا معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: براق د عربي نوم دی چې د 'ب-ر-ق' د ريښې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د رڼا یا شديدې رڼا معنی لري. په قرآن کریم کې، دا نوم د معراج شپه کې د رسول الله صلی الله علیه وسلم د سفر په تړاو ذکر شوی دی. په اسلامي کلتور کې، براق د برښنا یا چټکې رڼا نښه ده، او د الهي نور یا رباني اشراق سره تړاو لري.

in_english.name: Baraq
in_english.meaning: Baraq means light, brilliant light or flashing light
in_english.long_meaning: Baraq is an Arabic name derived from the root 'b-r-q', signifying light, brilliant light, or flashing light. It is mentioned in the Quran in reference to the Prophet Muhammad's nocturnal journey to Jerusalem. In Islamic tradition, Baraq symbolizes divine light, spiritual illumination, and enlightenment. The name carries strong religious and cultural significance across Muslim communities worldwide.

historical_references.reference: Baraq ibn Malik was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the Ten Promised Paradise. He participated in several major battles, including the Battle of Badr and the Battle of Uhud. He was known for his bravery and generosity, and was often referred to as 'Baraqah al-Ashjami' or 'Baraqah the Lightning of Ashjaa'.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, Battle of Badr and Battle of Uhud

historical_references.reference: Baraq ibn Al-Aahad was a poet and scholar from the Banu Hanifah tribe in pre-Islamic Arabia. He is known for his collection of poetry and his role in the development of Arabic literature. His poems often dealt with themes of love, nature, and the passing of time, and were highly influential in the development of classical Arabic poetry.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Baraq' in Islamic tradition is associated with a blessed night, where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) received revelations from Allah SWT. In modern context, this name is used in various domains. In astronomy, the 'Baraqah meteor shower' is named after this night. In weather forecasting, some meteorologists refer to a specific weather phenomenon, the 'Baraq storm', which is a heavy, prolonged thunderstorm. Technologically, 'Baraq' is used as a name for a high-speed internet service provider in some countries. The name is also used in Islamic calendar apps to denote the night of Barakah. Additionally, 'Baraq' is a popular name in social media, particularly among Arabic speakers, and is often used as a username or handle.
